races.name: Weatherbys Flat Horses To Follow Handicap

runners_data.name: Tenzi
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning to turf after AW success but facing tougher handicap company on 29 days rest
runners_data.spotlight: Went fairly close on her debut at Goodwood (6f, good) in June and just held on to open her account at Southwell (7f, AW) in March; handicap debut wasn't so good when back at 6f (AW) one month ago but it's still early days.

runners_data.name: Nifty
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with proven 6f form on similar going, headgear applied suggests connections expect improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Promising juvenile who won Chelmsford maiden (AW; second start) in June and fairly valuable Salisbury novice (again 6f, good to firm) three weeks later; signed off last term with solid handicap third but worryingly she finished last in both starts this spring; drops in grade with blinkers given a whirl and needs to prove she's trained on.

runners_data.name: Argy Bhaji
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent performer making turf handicap debut after encouraging second at Yarmouth on good to firm
runners_data.spotlight: Fairly consistent when placed in three AW qualifying starts and it was an encouraging handicap/turf debut when second of seven at Yarmouth (again 6f, good to firm) last month; probably capable of better and he's respected.

runners_data.name: King Of Chaos
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose best form came when making all but recent efforts suggest he's better waiting in rear
runners_data.spotlight: Made all to win Lingfield maiden (7f, AW) in February but his subsequent handicap form doesn't bare similar inspection, including when beating one home at Newmarket (6f, good) a fortnight ago; falling mark the straw to clutch at.

runners_data.name: Grey Horizon
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with strong AW record who showed return to form last time when dropped back to 6f, wearing visor
runners_data.spotlight: Enjoyed a fine spell on AW during the winter, winning four consecutive handicaps at 6f across January and February; came back to form when returned to 6f with third of 14 at Windsor (good to firm) on Saturday; same mark (due to go up 2lb) and this is less competitive.

runners_data.name: Jane Of The Jungle
runners_data.note: Natural front runner carrying 9lb weight advantage but remains a maiden after 11 attempts despite consistent placing
runners_data.spotlight: 11-race maiden but she went close at Southwell (AW) in March and finished on the heels of the principals when fourth of five in a blanket finish at Chepstow (also 5f, good to soft) last Thursday; more exposed than some of these but she stays 6f and can't be ruled out, albeit yard may have better prospects with Grey Horizon.

races.paceDynamic: Jane Of The Jungle is the only confirmed front runner in this small field of six, meaning she can dictate terms without pressure from flag to finish. Tenzi, Argy Bhaji and Grey Horizon will likely sit prominent but none are natural pace-pressers, creating a sustainable tempo throughout. The modest early gallop will set up a sprint finish from the 2f pole where stamina and tactical positioning become crucial. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses like Nifty and King Of Chaos who can benefit from the slow early pace and finish fastest when it matters.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Lead Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Jane Of The Jungle gets an easy lead and kicks clear early in the straight
scenarios.body: The modest early pace allows her to conserve energy before finding extra when challenged, while the prominent runners struggle to peg back her advantage. Her 9lb weight advantage becomes telling in the final furlong as fresher legs prevail.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow and becomes a sprint from 2f out
scenarios.body: Nifty and King Of Chaos get the perfect setup to unleash their finishing kicks from the rear, sweeping past the modest pace-setters. The strong finishers capitalize on conserved energy while prominent runners flatten out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pressure Tells
scenarios.trigger: If Tenzi or Grey Horizon apply sustained pressure from 3f out
scenarios.body: The early pace quickens enough to stretch Jane Of The Jungle's stamina while keeping the hold-up horses too far back. Grey Horizon's recent form improvement and Argy Bhaji's consistency shine through in a tactical battle.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If Jane Of The Jungle stops quickly and creates a blanket finish
scenarios.body: The race becomes a lottery as all six runners arrive together in the final 100 yards. King Of Chaos finds his best form while Tenzi benefits from Saffie Osborne's big-race experience in a photo finish.

watchPoints.text: Jane Of The Jungle getting a soft uncontested lead through the first half-mile with no pace pressure applied
Nifty and King Of Chaos being positioned too far back if the early pace is genuinely strong
Grey Horizon's ability to reproduce his AW form on turf given his disappointing recent efforts on the surface
Christian Howarth's 3lb claim being negated if Jane Of The Jungle gets too keen in front early
The draw impact on this tight Brighton track with hold-up horses potentially caught wide without cover

runners_data.name: High Calibre
runners_data.comment: 42,000gns yearling; first foal; dam German 1m 2yo winner; betting could be informative
runners_data.spotlight: 82,000gns February foal by Lucky Vega whose priced dropped to 42,000gns as a yearling; dam German 1m 2yo winner, half-sister to winners Grocer Jack (German/Italian 1m2f Group 3) and Ghislaine (German 7f Listed), out of German 1m3f Group 3 winner from family of Gold Cup winner Fame And Glory; likely to do better over further in time but is still considered from respected yard.

runners_data.name: Extended Order
runners_data.spotlight: Already-gelded April (fourth) foal by Without Parole; dam unplaced 1m1f-13.5f in France, closely related to 1m2f-1m4f winner Swiftsure, half-sister to US 1m3f Grade 2 winner Expansion, out of French 10.5f Group 3 winner; heed any market clues on this debut.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Beach
runners_data.comment: 62,000gns breeze-up purchase from a yard no stranger to first-time-out success
runners_data.spotlight: 62,000gns breeze-up 2yo; half-sister to four winners including So Majestic (Listed-placed 5f; RPR 97); dam 1m AW winner (88), half-sister to 6f/7f Group 3 winner Majestic Queen; 11-2 for novice at Ripon (6f, good) yesterday but always behind and beaten 11l.

runners_data.name: Terry O
runners_data.spotlight: February foal who did well in a messy debut when fourth at Bath (5f; Sayidah Ardad behind) this month and backed that up when fifth of 12 at Windsor (6f, also good) 11 days ago; again had some excuses last time and he has the makings of a nice type, particularly when things go a little more smoothly.

runners_data.name: Sayidah Ardad
runners_data.spotlight: March (first) foal; £4,000 yearling; looked to need the experience when seventh of ten at Bath (5f, good; Terry O fourth) 25 days ago; should do better.

runners_data.name: C'Est Lui
runners_data.spotlight: Early-May foal who was far from disgraced at 100-1 on his debut at Bath in late April but still looked green when weakening into midfield at Redcar (6f, good) 11 days ago; still early days.

races.name: Download The Fairplay App Now "Confined" Handicap (For Horses Which Have Not Won A Race In 2026)

runners_data.name: Abando
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 106 days off with Saffie Osborne taking valuable weight allowance
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-German runner who is another to have contested a Derby, in his case when beaten less than 10l in the Hamburg version in July; nowhere near that form in two starts for Marco Botti (including once in cheekpieces) and similar story on both outings for this yard; gelding operation, handicap debut and a mark in freefall put him top of the market watchlist, though.

runners_data.name: Maasai Mara
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who showed encouragement in hood on recent Wolverhampton return for John O'Shea
runners_data.spotlight: Regressed over hurdles last year but there was some encouragement with a hood deployed when fourth of seven at Wolverhampton (1m4f, AW) on his Flat return last month; blinkers (retained) were back on when a pace bias and wide draw did for him at Chester three weeks ago; not entirely ruled out.

runners_data.name: Golden Circet
runners_data.note: Strong closer with three turf wins including course success, returning from wind surgery
runners_data.spotlight: Three-time turf winner, including when just fending off OJ Lifestyle at Epsom (extended 1m, good; first-time visor) in July; following wind surgery he stuck at it from the rear when fifth over 1m2f (AW) last month and has run well over this trip previously; mark fine and he needs considering.

runners_data.name: Oj Lifestyle
runners_data.note: Three-time Brighton winner over 1m with excellent course form, suited by this distance extension
runners_data.spotlight: Three wins here (1m, good to firm), most recently in October, immediately raise interest and he stuck at it when third over 1m2f on his final start of last term; quiet reappearance in February probably best ignored and he's worth another go at this trip (tried once two years ago); respected.

runners_data.name: Kimeko Glory
runners_data.note: Recent yard change to Charles Hills with encouraging 1m4f debut run in blinkers last time
runners_data.spotlight: Won three times at 1m2f (good/good to firm) in her time with Mark Walford and Brian Toomey last year; encouraging start at 1m4f for this yard and first-time blinkers worked a little too well when a still-respectable fourth of 15 at Newbury (good) a fortnight ago; can do better wearing that aid for the second time.

runners_data.name: Rogue Impact
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who ran well over this trip at Thirsk, looking for first win since maiden success
runners_data.spotlight: Highly tried after winning Lingfield maiden (AW) in April last year and he bounced back from a swing at the Derby when going close at Thirsk (also 1m4f, good) in July; that form would make him a handicap snip but it's been a real struggle since and blinkers are now reached for; only considered if the market warms to him.

runners_data.name: Gallant Lion
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with course-and-distance form, reunited with Ian Williams after yard switch
runners_data.spotlight: 1m2f win here (good to firm) kicked off a four-timer in 2023 for Tony Carroll but he took a while to rediscover his level before scoring at Chepstow (1m4f, good; first-time blinkers) for this yard one year ago; raced mainly over further without success since and latest start over 1m can be written off; handy mark and he's not discounted on just his second visit to Brighton.

runners_data.name: Mister Daydream
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner returning after 225-day break, now 8lb below last winning mark
runners_data.spotlight: Went back-to-back (1m2f/1m3f on a sound surface) for Charlie Johnston last spring and is now 8lb below the latter winning mark after some lesser efforts for that yard; picked up for 1,000gns in October and is another to keep an eye on in the betting on this stable debut.

races.paceDynamic: Mister Daydream will lead this field with Gallant Lion likely to track in second, creating a genuine but not fierce pace over the 1m4f trip. With only one confirmed front runner and seven hold-up horses, the early gallop should be controlled and sustainable, allowing the field to remain bunched turning for home. This race shape heavily favours hold-up horses who can produce a strong finish, as they'll get the perfect setup from a moderate pace that won't stretch the field early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustained Hold-Up Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Mister Daydream sets a steady pace with Gallant Lion tracking close.
scenarios.body: The large pack of hold-up horses will get ideal conditions to unleash late runs, with the moderate early pace ensuring stamina reserves for the final 2f climb. Quality closers with proven form at this trip will have every chance to strike.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Pair Steal March
scenarios.trigger: If Mister Daydream and Gallant Lion stretch clear turning in while others wait too long.
scenarios.body: The leaders get first run on the field and maintain their advantage up Brighton's testing hill finish, holding off the late challengers who leave their runs too late. Gallant Lion's course form becomes decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Race Pressure Changes
scenarios.trigger: If Gallant Lion or another prominent runner applies unexpected early pressure to Mister Daydream.
scenarios.body: The pace quickens significantly from halfway, stretching the field and exposing any fitness doubts among the hold-up horses returning from breaks. Those with recent runs and proven stamina benefit from the stronger gallop.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the pace completely collapses with Mister Daydream going too slowly and multiple horses challenging together.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a tactical crawl before erupting into a blanket finish where track position and jockey timing matter more than form. Any horse can win in the resulting lottery.

watchPoints.text: Mister Daydream sets too strong a pace early given his 225-day absence, compromising his stamina for the hill finish
Golden Circet and Oj Lifestyle clash in the final furlong given their previous close encounter at Epsom
Kimeko Glory settles better in first-time blinkers for new trainer Charles Hills
Gallant Lion gets squeezed for room turning in given the large field of hold-up horses converging
Any horse making an early move from the back given the likely strong pace scenario

runners_data.name: Lady Of The Isles
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who needs a strong pace but looks best of the closers with hood producing career-best effort last year
runners_data.spotlight: Signed off last year with best effort yet when fourth of 15 at Leicester (1m2f, good; first-time hood) in October; two runs in blinkers this month haven't seen her return in the same form but the handicapper's starting to relent and this is winnable.

runners_data.name: Aim For The Bull
runners_data.note: Versatile hold-up performer who acts on turf despite recent AW success and suits the likely stamina emphasis at this trip
runners_data.spotlight: Dual AW scorer who picked up the second of those wins at Kempton (1m) in March; two solid AW runs followed and he should be fine back on turf, having placed in a course classified (1m, good to firm) in July; player.

runners_data.name: Joycean Way
runners_data.note: Blinkered hold-up horse who won here before and can track leaders better than most, ideally positioned for pace collapse scenarios
runners_data.spotlight: Blinkered when he hit a run of second spots at 7f and 1m last summer, including here (soft; acts on good to firm) in September; had previously looked unlucky on a couple of those occasions and the blinkers were absent when never figuring at Lingfield ten days ago; might do better with that aid now refitted and he's dangerously handicapped; watch the market.

runners_data.name: Havana Mojito
runners_data.note: Three-time Brighton winner who makes the pace but disappointed in this race last year when odds-on favourite
runners_data.comment: Below his last winning mark and he could build on last month's encouraging comeback run
runners_data.spotlight: Three-time course winner (7f/1m) who disappointed in this race last year when chasing a Brighton hat-trick; bounced back when runner-up at Epsom next time but he 's not been in the same form since, including when fifth at Leicester on Monday; body of work at this venue says he can never be dismissed, however, and first-time blinkers might reignite the fire.

runners_data.name: Rovinia
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare whose form has declined markedly since October breakthrough but gets significant weight relief from claim
runners_data.comment: 7f AW win last October came off 2lb higher; quiet this year and stamina a concern
runners_data.spotlight: Started well for this yard and her good run of form led to breakthrough win at Kempton (7f, AW) in October; struggled over a variety of trips on her last five starts, however, including from this career-low mark at Bath on Tuesday.

runners_data.name: Banksman
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer having first start for new yard after 146-day break, previously effective over this course and distance
runners_data.spotlight: Finished second both previous starts over C&D and also won two classified events when trained by Jack Channon; well beaten in two starts on the Flat since joining this stable, however, and was pulled up over hurdles 40 days ago; others preferred.

runners_data.name: Celebrating Ethel
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up mare who won a Brighton classified last year but recent form suggests decline setting in
runners_data.spotlight: Landed her second win on turf when picking up 1m2f course classified in August; similar trip and grade when winning at Wolverhampton (AW) in March but two lesser efforts followed; drops back in distance.

runners_data.name: Celtic John
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who was second over course and distance on only previous visit and won at Lingfield in January
runners_data.spotlight: Only start here produced a second over C&D (good to soft) in October and he got off the mark in a Lingfield classified (1m, AW) in January; not quite matched that in three starts since and yet to prove he's effective on quick turf; still can't be ruled out in a moderate contest.

runners_data.name: Unknown Journey
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who is 0-23 but adds early pace pressure despite recent poor form for in-form Tony Carroll yard
runners_data.spotlight: 0-23 and after going close in a Lingfield classified in February he's been way off that in three subsequent starts, including when tailed off last time.

runners_data.name: Manton Road
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who won four times on AW last year but has disappointed since yard switch under cloud
runners_data.spotlight: Won four times on AW in the first three months of last year for Gay Kelleway but left that yard under a cloud and hasn't built on encouraging first go for this stable in March; work to do on his return to turf.

runners_data.name: Weston Court
runners_data.note: Front runner whose visor is back on but has habit of fading in finish and trailed field three times recently
runners_data.spotlight: Cheekpieces were on for both of his wins in the summer of 2024 but he's generally struggled in that aid since and trailed the field on three of his last four starts; newly fitted visor needs to prompt a big revival.

races.paceDynamic: Havana Mojito and Weston Court are the confirmed front runners but Weston Court has a concerning habit of fading late which could leave Havana Mojito with an easier lead than ideal. Unknown Journey adds some pace pressure from a prominent position but the overall gallop looks modest rather than fierce. With most of the field comprising hold-up horses including Joycean Way, Aim For The Bull, and Lady Of The Isles, this sets up as a race where the pace could collapse in the final two furlongs. This moderate pace scenario strongly favours horses that can track the leaders and kick, disadvantaging pure hold-up horses who need a strong gallop to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Collapses
scenarios.trigger: If Havana Mojito gets an easy lead when Weston Court fades and the pace slackens significantly
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the two-furlong pole where horses tracking the pace have the decisive advantage over those held up at the back. Prominent runners and those able to position handy benefit most from the tactical setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Genuine Gallop Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Unknown Journey puts real pressure on the leaders and creates a true staying test from halfway
scenarios.body: The honest pace allows the hold-up horses to close strongly and the front runners get found out for stamina late. Pure closers with proven stamina benefit most from the strong early gallop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Early Speed Duel
scenarios.trigger: If Havana Mojito and Unknown Journey engage in a sustained battle for the lead through the middle stages
scenarios.body: Both pace angles get compromised leaving the race to horses that can sit third or fourth and benefit from the pace collapse. Mid-division runners profit most from the early speed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Crawling Pace Setup
scenarios.trigger: If all the front runners go too slowly and create a tactical crawl through the first half-mile
scenarios.body: The race becomes purely about who has the most speed in the final quarter-mile regardless of official ratings. Raw pace from any position becomes the key factor over stamina.

watchPoints.text: Weston Court typically fades badly in the final furlong which could leave Havana Mojito with an uncontested lead if Unknown Journey doesn't apply enough early pressure
Joycean Way in blinkers can improve significantly for the return to Brighton where he was second in this race previously and benefits most from pace collapse
Aim For The Bull returning to turf after solid AW form and Rob Hornby's 1/8 strike rate for Mike Murphy suggests confidence in transition back to grass
Lady Of The Isles showed career-best form in hood last year but recent blinkers runs have been poor, watch for return to headgear that worked
Unknown Journey's prominent style crucial to pace dynamics despite poor recent form as he's the main threat to give leaders pressure early

runners_data.name: Dalmally
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with poor recent form who flopped badly as favorite on his return to this course last time
runners_data.spotlight: Won a 2yo course maiden (good to soft) in 2024 but flopped on his return visit when favourite for a handicap (also 1m, good to firm; first-time blinkers) last September; left Hughie Morrison after another lesser effort and that pattern has continued in three starts for this yard; hopes probably pinned on this drop back in trip.

runners_data.name: My Boy Harry
runners_data.note: Classic hold-up horse in excellent form with recent wins on turf; quick turnaround from Tuesday success
runners_data.spotlight: Mostly campaigned on AW but he's now 2-9 on turf having landed C&D classified (good to firm) in June and Lingfield handicap (7f, good) last Tuesday; took advantage of a golden highway that day but did well to pick his way through from the rear and he's respected under a 5lb penalty (1lb well in).

runners_data.name: Zu Run
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who won at this C&D last May but has been disappointing in recent outings
runners_data.spotlight: First visit here proved a winning one when taking handicap over this trip (good to firm) last May; flopped on his second go one month later and only bits and pieces of form since; career-low mark and cheekpieces (0-3) make a return after two-year absence.

runners_data.name: Kondratiev Wave
runners_data.note: Veteran prominent runner in good form this year; reliable at this level but aging at nine years old
runners_data.spotlight: In the veteran stage now but the old man's been giving younger legs plenty of trouble this year, dead-heating at Lingfield (7f, AW) in February and placed on another five occasions; still in good heart judged on latest second at Bath (1m, firm) and this dual C&D winner can go well again.

runners_data.name: Havana Joy
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner returning after 38-day break; unproven over this trip but Charles Hills stable
runners_data.spotlight: Unraced at two; yet to score but she was placed in her first five starts (6f/7f, AW) last year; 196-day break preceded a poor effort in November, however, and wind surgery hasn't improved matters judged on two runs this year; tongue-tie and blinkers thrown into the mixer and she's dangerously handicapped if rediscovering her mojo on this turf debut.

runners_data.name: Valsharah
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who is a 23-race maiden despite some decent placed efforts; trying tongue-tie today
runners_data.spotlight: 23-race maiden who has tried various headgear (including combinations) since joining this yard but it was only today's tongue-tie he sported when close second at Kempton (6f, AW) in March; career-low mark and he's a contender if subsequent efforts can be forgiven.

runners_data.name: Dion Baker
runners_data.note: Front-running specialist 20lb lower than his C&D winning mark; key contender if pace doesn't kill him
runners_data.spotlight: Four wins include one over C&D (good) in May 2024; hasn't scored since August of that year but he's now 20lb lower and latest fourth of 13 at Doncaster (7f, good to soft) was a solid effort despite hanging; should enhance creditable Brighton form figures of 21424.

runners_data.name: Regal Guest
runners_data.note: Front-runner with Harry Burns taking valuable 3lb claim; disappointing recent form and ran yesterday
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced 4yo but he's beaten only one rival in three handicaps; cheekpieces added
runners_data.spotlight: Third at Kempton (7f, AW) last March on second start but uninspiring in his four handicaps, latest with first-time cheekpieces at Yarmouth yesterday.

races.paceDynamic: Havana Joy, Regal Guest, and Dion Baker will ensure a strong gallop from the off, with all three naturally wanting to lead in this small field. The pace will be genuinely testing over 7f on good to firm ground, likely stringing out the field and putting stamina at a premium. With three confirmed front-runners battling for position early, the pace should be honest throughout. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses and those with proven stamina who can finish strongly off the strong pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Benefits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners engage in early pace warfare as expected
scenarios.body: The honest gallop will set up perfectly for the hold-up brigade who can pick off tired leaders in the final furlong. My Boy Harry and Zu Run both have the tactical speed to capitalize from their patient styles.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives Battle
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace-setters can steal a march and find just enough breathing room
scenarios.body: Dion Baker drops to his lowest mark in years and his C&D win last May shows he can handle this exact scenario. His 20lb drop in the weights could prove decisive if the pace isn't suicidal.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong but not suicidal, allowing a prominent runner to track and pounce
scenarios.body: Kondratiev Wave and Valsharah can sit just off the pace and have the tactical nous to strike when the leaders tire. The veteran Kondratiev Wave has been running well in similar scenarios this year.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners neutralize each other too early and the pace becomes moderate
scenarios.body: A more sedate gallop would compromise the hold-up horses and potentially favor the prominent runners who can quicken. However, with three natural leaders this scenario seems highly unlikely.

watchPoints.text: Regal Guest running just 24 hours after yesterday's Yarmouth effort could show severe signs of fatigue
Havana Joy making her first appearance for 38 days and unproven beyond 7f may struggle with stamina demands
Dion Baker's front-running style in a pace battle could see him burn out badly in the final furlong
My Boy Harry's quick return from Tuesday's Lingfield win but his hold-up style should suit this pace setup
Zu Run wearing a hood for the first time which could either help or hinder his concentration levels

runners_data.name: On Key
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has shown consistency over 7f but needs to prove 6f effectiveness on turf
runners_data.spotlight: 0-19 and modest form nowadays; also down the weights and followed three competitive 7f efforts on AW with a fair show in big field on turf last time, but this first visit to Brighton needs to spark something extra from him.

runners_data.name: Starsong
runners_data.note: Low-drawn prominent runner with strong Brighton record including two wins from similar positions
runners_data.spotlight: Fared well from low draws at this track last year, including for two wins, and she's been close up at other tracks on two of her four starts this year; drawn high this time but has to be seriously considered.

runners_data.name: Dark Sun
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose Windsor fourth suggests she retains place claims despite winless record
runners_data.spotlight: 0-17 record includes a near miss over 7f last summer and two over 6f early this year; Windsor 6f fourth three weeks ago confirms her place claims but it's not surprising that connections now reach for cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Neptune Legend
runners_data.note: Fresh from impressive Bath win for Tony Carroll, suits hold-up style in tactical races
runners_data.spotlight: Third run back with Tony Carroll when taking advantage of his reduced mark at Bath (5.7f) last Friday and he did it in good style; that gives him a big chance under just a 4lb penalty but he's run with credit at Brighton only once from eight visits.

runners_data.name: Thanks Dad
runners_data.note: Consistent Brighton performer racing prominently but carrying modest current form
runners_data.spotlight: Fourth on all four appearances at Brighton; 29 races overall, with both his wins on Southwell AW last March/September; thrown in on that form but he was out of form this winter and on recent return to turf after five months off; others have more pressing claims.

runners_data.name: Bated Breeze
runners_data.note: Returns after 211-day break with David Egan booking suggesting stable confidence
runners_data.spotlight: 0-18, with his solitary second over 7f on soft; ended 2025 with two respectable thirds in October, including over 7f here on good to firm, but first time out has seen two of his best shows, so he needs a second look today.

runners_data.name: Top Biller
runners_data.note: Front runner who showed improved form when second at Yarmouth racing more patiently
runners_data.spotlight: Most of his best efforts have come from the front but he just raced in touch when second at Yarmouth (6f) on latest outing, his best show this year; well handicapped if judged on peak 2025 efforts.

runners_data.name: Secret Handsheikh
runners_data.note: Brighton specialist returning quickly after moderate effort, best over shorter trips
runners_data.spotlight: The latest of his 11 wins was last August off 5lb higher; no win over this far since 2021 but he goes well at this track and, despite recent form, can't be comfortably ruled out.

runners_data.name: Port Hedland
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll-trained runner whose only win came over Brighton's extended 5f trip
runners_data.spotlight: The extended 5f at Brighton (good to firm) last May brought his only win from 27 races; his most competitive shows since were on AW this March but he was second favourite on return to turf at Bath last Friday, only to be hampered; not entirely dismissed.

runners_data.name: Henry Tudor
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning from 79-day break with cheekpieces and tongue-tie applied
runners_data.spotlight: Well backed when firmly on top in a 6f classified event at Chelmsford (AW) in February but that's the only time he's not been well held; usual accessories were left off that day, as they were in a handicap in March on his only start since; form case depends on that one run and this is turf debut.

runners_data.name: Voodoo Ray
runners_data.note: Former Brighton winner but poor recent form suggests decline from peak ability
runners_data.spotlight: The first four of his five wins were at Brighton but no success anywhere since May 2024; discouraging record from autumn 2024 onwards.

runners_data.name: Lynwood Lad
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with one Brighton win but inconsistent record at the track
runners_data.spotlight: Won a 5.5f classified on the first of his two visits to Brighton (last summer) but ran poorly in the other; latest start was easily his best in 2026 but that was in March and he's inconsistent.

runners_data.name: Lil Wade
runners_data.note: Limited turf performer who fades in finish and faces stronger opposition than usual
runners_data.spotlight: This is only his third race on turf but he finished last and second last in the others; none of his 2025 or 2026 form reads well enough and his 0-33 overall record is probably the bottom line.

races.paceDynamic: Top Biller stands as the sole confirmed front runner, likely to get his own way on the lead without serious pressure from the prominent racers like On Key, Starsong, and Thanks Dad. The moderate early gallop will allow the field to stay compact through the first half, before quickening in the final 2f where stamina and tactical positioning become crucial. With minimal pace pressure and a likely sprint finish developing, this race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce late kicks and prominent racers with tactical speed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustainable Pace Suits Finishers
scenarios.trigger: If Top Biller leads uncontested and the pace stays steady through halfway
scenarios.body: The lack of early burn allows hold-up horses to stay closer than usual and unleash telling strikes in the final furlong. Late-running types get perfect conditions to show their turn of foot when it matters most.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group of On Key, Starsong and Thanks Dad press Top Biller early
scenarios.body: A faster tempo stretches the field and exposes the stamina limitations of pure hold-up horses. Those racing handy throughout can kick clear before the back markers can respond effectively.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Top Biller gets soft fractions and finds extra gear when challenged
scenarios.body: His early advantage combined with the testing Brighton hill proves decisive as challengers fail to peg him back. The sustained pace from 2f out plays to his front-running strengths perfectly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Benefits Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a messy sprint from 3f out
scenarios.body: The stop-start nature negates class differences and allows a well-positioned longshot to steal through. Form horses get caught in traffic while an unfancied runner finds daylight at the right moment.

watchPoints.text: Top Biller could steal this if he gets uncontested fractions and the field allows him too much rope early
Neptune Legend's quick return after Bath win suggests connections think he can follow up under similar conditions
Starsong's low draw gives her tactical advantage she has exploited successfully at Brighton before
Several Moore runners including Bated Breeze returning from breaks could outrun their odds if fit enough
The 3lb claiming riders on Dark Sun and Thanks Dad add extra pressure in a competitive handicap

races.name: Streamline Taxis 202020 Dash From The Stalls Handicap

runners_data.name: Coolagh Magic
runners_data.note: Hold-up veteran dangerously well handicapped but 0-21 on turf with 50 days off
runners_data.spotlight: Veteran who is 9-46 on the AW and 0-21 on grass, but he has become dangerously well handicapped on the pick of his turf form last year; should find this race is run to suit.

runners_data.name: Wedgewood
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner who is 6-24 on the AW and just 1-18 on turf, though she ran well when second of seven at Bath (5f, firm) 16 days ago and races off the same mark; likely to face competition for the lead, but she comes into this in better heart than most.

runners_data.name: Hi Hoh Tonto
runners_data.note: Front-runner on 0-21 losing streak who won't get uncontested lead against Coast
runners_data.spotlight: 0-21; likes to front-run, but he isn't alone in that regard in this field.

runners_data.name: Dreambird Dolly
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with strong 3/5 C&D placing record, new headgear combination applied
runners_data.spotlight: 0-17, but she has been placed in three of her five starts over C&D so can be given an each-way shout; new headgear combination.

runners_data.name: Kento
runners_data.note: Prominent AW specialist 0-9 on turf, wide draw compromises his usual forward position
runners_data.spotlight: All three wins at Wolverhampton (5f, AW) including two this year; 0-9 on turf, though, and an easy lead seems unlikely, especially from a wide draw; stable also runs Wedgewood.

runners_data.name: Rainbow Sorbet
runners_data.note: Hold-up type making stable debut after 39 days off, minimal turf experience
runners_data.spotlight: Third in his only outing for Michael O'Callaghan at Gowran Park (1m, good) a year ago, but nothing in two starts at Lingfield (6f, AW) since returning for this yard in March; makes handicap debut in a first-time visor; probably best watched unless market suggests otherwise; stable also runs Almavillalobas.

runners_data.name: Barnsnape Boy
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who won easily here last August, poor fresh record forgives Windsor effort
runners_data.spotlight: Doesn't have a great record fresh so this month's Windsor reappearance isn't hard to forgive; won easily from 2lb lower over C&D (good) last August having made all, but similar tactics won't be easy in this field, especially from the widest stall.

runners_data.name: Apple's Angel
runners_data.note: Prominent runner making yard debut after 256 days off, better over longer trips
runners_data.spotlight: 3-14 on the AW for Simon Dow and 0-7 on turf; may need this first start for her new trainer after 256 days off and is probably better over a bit further now.

runners_data.name: Battle Point
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with 1-49 career record, some C&D frame form but chronic winning issues
runners_data.spotlight: Has made the frame a few times over C&D, but a record of 1-49 doesn't make him an appealing proposition.

runners_data.name: Coast
runners_data.note: Only confirmed front-runner from rail draw, 26-race losing run but recent Bath form solid
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner who ran well when fourth of 13 at Bath (5.7f, good to firm) a week ago, but her losing run is up to 26 and she's unlikely to get her own way in this field.

runners_data.name: Almavillalobas
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with chronic finishing problems, visor removed after poor recent efforts
runners_data.spotlight: Has shown very little in nine starts from 5f-11.4f; visor removed; makes no appeal.

races.paceDynamic: Coast is the only confirmed front-runner, giving her a clear tactical advantage to dictate terms from the rail. Wedgewood (non-runner) and Hi Hoh Tonto also like to lead but Coast should get first run, with Kento, Dreambird Dolly tracking in behind from prominent positions. The lack of pace pressure means Coast can set sustainable fractions before the field closes late. This setup strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can position close to the pace without having to fight for it.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Coast Controls Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Coast breaks cleanly and faces no early pressure for the lead
scenarios.body: She dictates comfortable fractions and has enough left to resist late challenges on this sharp 5½f trip. The lack of pace pressure allows her to conserve energy for the finish despite her long losing run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Kento or Dreambird Dolly settle perfectly behind the pace and find clear room
scenarios.body: They get the perfect trip tracking Coast's moderate gallop before unleashing superior finishing kicks. Dreambird Dolly's strong C&D record and Kento's class advantage tell late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finds Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes crawling and Coolagh Magic gets a dream run through
scenarios.body: The veteran's dangerous handicap mark finally comes into play as he finds daylight in the straight. His improving form pattern suggests he's primed for a big effort despite the surface concerns.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Coast ties up badly and multiple horses challenge simultaneously in a bunched finish
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from 2f out with hold-up horses benefiting from the strong pace collapse. Long shots with tactical speed get competitive in a blanket finish.

watchPoints.text: Coast must break alertly from stall 1 to establish her crucial early lead before Hi Hoh Tonto can challenge
Dreambird Dolly needs clean passage from mid-division as her C&D record depends on finding racing room
Kento's wide draw forces him to use energy early or settle further back than ideal for turf debut
Coolagh Magic requires genuine pace up front to set up his hold-up style on return to turf
Apple's Angel making first start for new trainer after 256 days may need this run despite headgear addition
